Cell3 uses ICRS columns [a b c], an intentional negative determinant, and half-open cells [-1/2,1/2)^3. Use x-O_K in affine reciprocal identities.

course_map.assessment_target: Compute node polarity without merging distinct meanings of parity

mod_three_bridge.introduce: Define lambda mod3 as its remainder0,1,2, using lambda=3k+r with integer k and0<=r<3. This is different from even/odd parity.
mod_three_bridge.worked: lambda=-2 has mod3 class1 and chi=+1; lambda=1 has the same class1 but chi=-1.
mod_three_bridge.practice: lambda=-1 has class2, chi=-1; lambda=2 has class2, chi=+1. Count nine nodes in each mod3 class from the seven sheet counts.
mod_three_bridge.diagnostic: The seven sheet populations give three mod3 populations9,9,9 but two chi populations13,14. Neither class label nor chi determines directed L. Retain each field separately.

course_map.assessment_target: Separate 26 noncentral nodes from 13 unoriented pairs

guided_practice.task_and_answer: L=(0,-1,-1) gives v=(0,1,1), s=-1; its partner has s=+1. Reconstruct both physical points and show their sum is 2O.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A pair label alone cannot recover directed L. Keep s and treat the center separately; do not assign it two orientations.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Synthetic unit interval [0,1): split into [0,1/2),[1/2,1), then four quarter intervals. Child indices j=0..3 at depth2 have parent floor(j/2).

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Depth3 child j=5 is [5/8,6/8), parent j=2 at depth2 and parent j=1 at depth1.

typed_count_bridge.worked: A centered window has3 half-step positions per axis, yielding27 nodes. A Lucas Group has3 complete cells per axis, yielding27 VOLUMES and outer basis3B. Draw a1D row with three cell centers and four boundary corners to distinguish nodes and volumes.
typed_count_bridge.practice: A9B Supergroup has9 complete cells per axis, hence729 VOLUMES, equivalently27 Groups of27 cells.
typed_count_bridge.diagnostic: Classify the numbers27(nodes),27(volumes),729(volumes) by object and unit; matching cardinalities do not identify their objects.

course_map.title: Dyadic geometry and triadic addresses
course_map.worked_example_capability: Distinguish the two source-defined recursion systems
course_map.assessment_target: Distinguish the two source-defined recursion systems

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Type two independent depth counters n2 and d3. Teach remainder modulo a positive integer using congruent examples including negatives. Do not identify a halving refinement with a ternary address.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For a synthetic group root 3B: dyadic n2=0 gives 27 cells, 64 vertices; n2=1 gives 216 cells,343 vertices. Ternary depth d3=1 has 27 address classes; d3=2 has729.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: One coordinate of A2 is represented by 0..8. Residue 7 reduces to1 modulo3; (-2) modulo3 also gives1. In 3D (7,5,0) maps to(1,2,0).

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Equal counts do not identify objects: 27 geometric volumes at n2=0 are not the same typed object as 27 ternary address classes at d3=1.

teaching_anchor.production_rule: Expand this anchor diagnostic to 3–5 diagnostic checks; teach all operations before use. Split the lesson if these activities exceed 55 minutes.

rung_equation_bridge.introduce: For this source equation only, g_rung and n_rung are nonnegative integers. They are not automatically the independently named dyadic depth n2 or ternary address depth d3.
rung_equation_bridge.worked: 3^g_rung*2^n_rung+1=10 becomes3^g_rung*2^n_rung=9. The right side is odd, so n_rung=0. Then3^g_rung=9, so g_rung=2.
rung_equation_bridge.practice: Bound g_rung<=2 and n_rung<=3 using monotone nonnegative powers, and check the12 candidate pairs; only(2,0) works.
rung_equation_bridge.diagnostic: State the domain before claiming uniqueness; identify how the resulting outer9B count729 differs from ternary residue cardinality27^2, despite their equal numbers.

course_map.title: Scaling length, area, and node counts
course_map.worked_example_capability: Derive quantity-specific scaling and shared-boundary counts
course_map.assessment_target: Derive quantity-specific scaling and shared-boundary counts

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Derive shared-boundary counts from vertices along each axis, and length/area/volume scaling from products. State which root stays fixed.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For fixed outer 3B, each depth-n2 subcell has basis 2^-n2 B; cells=27*8^n2 and merged corner vertices=(3*2^n2+1)^3. At n2=2:1728 cells,2197 vertices.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: From n2=1 to2, subcell length halves, face area quarters, volume divides by8; total occupied volume stays27*|det B|=162 synthetic length^3.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: At n2=1, 216*8=1728 counts cell-vertex incidences, not the343 distinct vertices. Explain shared vertices. Do not confuse B_(p,n)=3^p*2^-n B with the fixed outer group boundary.

supergroup_halfstep_bridge.introduce: An inclusive integer range from -m to m contains2m+1 values. Count a one-dimensional grid before taking its3D product. These are geometry half-step samples, not dyadic corner counts.
supergroup_halfstep_bridge.worked: A centered9B span has19 half-step positions per axis, labeled-9..9, giving19^3=6859 points. Integer lambda=i+j+k ranges from-27 to27, giving55 possible sheets. Every intermediate sum is attained: use one coordinate up to9, then a second, then a third; mirror for negative sums.
supergroup_halfstep_bridge.practice: The smaller3B span has labels-3..3, giving7^3=343 half-step points and lambda=-9..9, giving19 sheets; its complete-volume count is27.
supergroup_halfstep_bridge.diagnostic: For9B distinguish729 volumes,1000 ordinary boundary corners,6859 half-step points and55 sheets. State the sampling grid whenever quoting a count.
supergroup_halfstep_bridge.pacing: Use two55-minute periods for lesson-03: first dyadic shared-boundary/scaling counts, second half-step counts and sheet range. Preserve both practice/check sets.

course_map.assessment_target: Encode and decode finite signed-digit addresses

worked_example.task_and_answer: Digits (epsilon0,epsilon1,epsilon2)=(-1,0,1) represent8. Modulo27 that is class8; its depth2 reduction is class8 modulo9, represented by balanced digits(-1,0) with integer representative-1.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Integer5 has digits(-1,-1,1), since -1-3+9=5. At depth2 its balanced representative is-4, congruent to5 modulo9; at depth1 representative-1 is congruent to2 modulo3.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: The same residue can have different integer representatives. Recover a finite integer only when digit list and depth are retained; a reduced residue alone loses the high digit.

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Use two periods. First teach linearity, idempotence E(Ef)=Ef, range and the block-constant subalgebra in plain language. Then prove the two-sided block-factor rule E(b1*f*b2)=b1*E(f)*b2 for block-constant b1,b2. Show explicitly why an arbitrary idempotent map is insufficient.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Take f=(0,2,2,4), g=(1,1,0,2). Q(fg)=(-1,1,-4,4); compute the four RHS terms and verify equality. For block constant b=(2,2,-1,-1), verify E(b*f)=b*E(f).

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Define E_star(x,y,z)=(x,x,z+y-x). It is linear, fixes(1,1,1), is idempotent and has a multiplication-closed range(a,a,b), yet lacks the block-factor property. For b=(1,1,0),f=(0,1,0), E_star(b*f)=(0,0,1) while b*E_star(f)=0. With f=g=(0,1,0), Q_star(fg)=(0,1,-1) but the purported RHS=(0,1,-3). Identify the missing hypothesis.

teaching_anchor.production_requirement: These are blueprint anchors, not full lessons. Expand to2–4 observable goals and3–5 diagnostics, with worked answers. A failed prerequisite check triggers extra practice before dependent work; periods may expand.
line_by_line_derivation: Work in the real finite-array algebra with pointwise multiplication; the range B_coarse is a multiplication-closed subalgebra of arrays constant on each fixed block.

Declare E linear, E^2=E, E(1)=1, and E(b1*f*b2)=b1*E(f)*b2 for b1,b2 in B_coarse. Pair-block averaging has these properties: fixed block factors pull outside a finite average. Positivity also holds but is not needed for this displayed algebraic derivation.
Set qf=f-Ef and qg=g-Eg. Linearity and idempotence give E(qf)=E(qg)=0.
Apply E term by term. E(Ef*Eg)=Ef*Eg because the range is a subalgebra fixed by E; bimodule rules give E(Ef*qg)=0 and E(qf*Eg)=0.
Thus E(fg)=Ef*Eg+E(qf*qg); subtract this from the expansion to obtain Q(fg)=Ef*qg+qf*Eg+qf*qg-E(qf*qg).

The synthetic operator is a fully specified sufficient teaching model. The compressed S02 record does not itself supply a complete general E definition; S03 AUD-006 flags this. Do not claim this exercise retrieves or certifies an unspecified archival proof body.
